source_review.notes: Checked current ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 and 15288:2023 metadata; NASA Technical Requirements Definition and appendix guidance; SEBoK 2.14 System Requirements Definition; NIST SP 800-160 Volume 1 Revision 1 and CSF 2.0; and the official EUR-Lex text for Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. NASA, SEBoK, NIST, and EUR-Lex returned HTTP 200. Both ISO pages returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client; current official metadata was independently inspected during authoring, but command-line reachability is not claimed.

notation_and_syntax.notes: Every symbol is introduced before use. Source text, applicability facts, authorized interpretation, controlled obligation, engineered requirement, evidence, finding, and acceptance remain distinct.

Checked that applicability admits true, false, and controlled-undetermined states and that a finding remains bounded by evidence, scheme, configuration, time, and authority.

evidence: Reviewed jurisdiction and role changes, definitions/exemptions, effective and transition dates, official-language issues, dated incorporation, conflicting deletion/retention, supplier evidence, alternative means, emergency authorization, product-versus-organization allocation, remote access, changed intended use, AI classification, accessibility, medical-device process duties, and safety prohibitions.

conceptual_review.notes: Professor-style review checked constraint, regulatory requirement, applicability, normative source, guidance, standard, incorporation by reference, prescriptive/performance-based obligation, compliance, certification, assurance, deviation, waiver, alternative means, finding, allocation, and temporal validity for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Practitioner-style review checked data residency, standards contracts, medical-device organizational processes, accessibility, safety interlocks, cross-jurisdiction record conflict, supplier certification, cloud procurement, EU AI Act applicability, emergency authorization, incident notification, market profiles, and hospital scheduling. Each example exposes facts, assumptions, authority, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Pedagogical review confirmed progression from source inventory and authority through applicability, definitions/modality, allocation, translation, standards, evidence, supplier inheritance, conflict/deviation, security/safety, temporal change, and bounded automation. Ten examples and five complete answers require classification, applicability analysis, diagnosis, comparison, and high-consequence transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
